extra.message: POST /ops/bundle/loan-thaw-178 passes the raw request body (or the base64-decoded 'blob' query parameter) directly to pickle.loads() with no validation or type checking. pickle is not safe for untrusted input: a crafted pickle payload executes arbitrary code during deserialization, giving remote code execution on the server.

GET /ops/formula/loan-cast-261 passes the user-controlled 'expr' query parameter directly to eval(). Supplying {'__builtins__': {}} does not make eval safe (literals, attribute chains and comprehensions remain reachable), so an attacker can evaluate arbitrary Python expressions and achieve remote code execution.

GET /ops/jinja/loan-cast-583 constructs a Jinja2 template from the user-controlled 'fragment' query parameter (Template("Result: " + fragment).render()) and returns the rendered output as HTML. Because the template string itself is attacker-controlled, this is server-side template injection; payloads can traverse __class__/__mro__/__subclasses__ to read files or execute code.

GET /ops/shell/loan-probe-635 builds a shell command by string concatenation, os.system("ping -c 1 " + host), using the user-controlled 'host' query parameter without sanitization. Shell metacharacters (e.g. ';', '|', '`') in 'host' execute arbitrary OS commands on the server.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: POST /ops/xml/loan-fold-614 parses the raw request body with lxml using etree.XMLParser(load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False) and etree.fromstring(). External entity declarations and DTDs are resolved with network access enabled, allowing local file disclosure via file:// URIs and SSRF to internal services (XXE).

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: POST /ops/dock/loan-shelf-594 builds the destination path as BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name from the user-controlled 'name' parameter with no traversal sanitization, creates parent directories, and writes the request body with target.write_bytes(body). A name containing '../' sequences escapes the export directory, allowing arbitrary file write/overwrite anywhere the process can write.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: GET /ops/blurb/loan-tile-326 renders the user-controlled 'card' query parameter through Template("{{ card|safe }}"). The |safe filter disables Jinja2 autoescaping and the result is returned as HTMLResponse, so arbitrary HTML/JavaScript supplied in 'card' executes in a victim's browser (reflected XSS).

GET /ops/after/loan-aftercard-069 returns RedirectResponse(lane) where 'lane' is the user-controlled query parameter with no allowlist or validation. An absolute URL such as http://evil.com turns the endpoint into an open redirect usable for phishing.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site (Open Redirect)

extra.message: POST /ops/workset/loan-rebind-203 seeds a workset with security-relevant attributes (role='viewer', approved=False, balance) and then blindly applies workset.update(payload) using the unvalidated request JSON. The client can overwrite role, approved, balance and any other attribute, bypassing the intended authorization defaults (mass assignment).

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: GET /ops/crumb/loan-lane-296 sets the 'portal_crumb' cookie from the user-controlled 'marker' query parameter via response.set_cookie("portal_crumb", marker) with no httponly, secure or samesite attributes. The cookie value is fully attacker-controlled and lacks every standard security flag, enabling cookie injection/fixation and script access to its value.

GET /ops/identity/loan-hint-555 authorizes access using handle/verifier pairs hardcoded in source: known = {'north': '4812', 'south': '5930'}. The verifiers are trivially brute-forceable 4-digit constants; the endpoint also leaks handle existence by returning 404 for unknown handles versus 403 for a bad verifier.

GET /ops/origin/loan-mirror-565 reflects the untrusted Origin request header directly into the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header and additionally sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. Any origin is therefore trusted for credentialed cross-origin reads, defeating the same-origin policy.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: GET /ops/frame/loan-slip-575 explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection: 0 and an empty Content-Security-Policy header, deliberately disabling the browser's XSS auditor and all content-security restrictions for this response.

GET /ops/nonce/loan-roll-605 generates the returned code with random.choice() from Python's random module (Mersenne Twister), which is not cryptographically secure. Tokens/codes produced this way are predictable after observing a few outputs; the secrets module must be used instead.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)
CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values

extra.message: GET /ops/badge/loan-gate-625 grants the elevated lane ('lane': 'elevated', payroll and casework data) based solely on the client-controlled 'ops_badge' cookie or 'x-ops-badge' header (badge == 'lead'). The badge value is never authenticated or validated server-side, so anyone can set it to obtain elevated results.

cwe: CWE-565: Reliance on Cookies without Validation and Integrity Checking

extra.message: GET /ops/trust/loan-drift-645 creates ssl._create_unverified_context() and passes it to urllib.request.urlopen for the outbound HTTPS request to the partner endpoint. TLS certificate verification is disabled, allowing a man-in-the-middle attacker to impersonate the partner and intercept or modify the exchange.

GET /ops/pulse/loan-packet-wobble-067 catches a raised RuntimeError and returns str(exc) and exc.__class__.__name__ to the client with status 500. The error text embeds the user-controlled 'lot_ref' value and the internal PRIVATE_EXPORT_DIR directory path, disclosing internal implementation details to remote callers.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: POST /ops/wire/loan-underwrite-roll-068 logs the entire request body and the Authorization header via logger.warning("underwriting intake body=%s auth=%s", ...). Credentials and sensitive payload data are persisted to application logs.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: POST /ops/delta/loan-nudge-135 applies client-supplied values to the ledger with no validation or bounds: ledger['balance'] -= amount accepts arbitrary values (including negative amounts that inflate the balance past the 900 limit), and ledger['state'] is overwritten directly from the request JSON, so the client fully controls the supposedly server-side ledger state.

GET /api/borrowers/{borrower_id} loads any borrower profile by the attacker-supplied id. Authorization is enforced only for the borrower (ownership) and underwriter (assignment) roles; support_specialist falls through the if/elif chain without any scope check and receives full borrower PII including tax_identifier_last4, owner phone/email and address (insecure direct object reference).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: PATCH /api/borrowers/{borrower_id} permits the support_specialist role to modify any borrower profile: the role allowlist at line 1275 includes 'support_specialist' with no object-level ownership or assignment check, and apply_profile_update(profile, payload) then writes attacker-chosen business_name, owner_email, owner_phone, address and other fields to the target profile.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: PATCH /api/applications/{application_id} authorizes staff only through require_application_view, which is a pass-through for support_specialist on every application. Unlike borrowers, staff face no editable-status restriction, so a support specialist can modify any application - including approved/rejected ones - changing product, requested_amount, purpose, term and the financial figures, and via payload.borrower_profile can also rewrite the target borrower's profile data.

POST /api/documents/{document_id}/upload only blocks underwriters and non-owning borrowers; require_application_view() returns True for support_specialist on every application (can_view_application). A support specialist can therefore upload and replace any borrower's KYC documents, including identity and tax documents, for applications they have no business editing.

application_detail() exposes internal underwriting notes and full payment-account details to every user for whom is_staff() is true, which includes support_specialist. Support staff therefore receive internal-only notes and borrower bank account data on every application they can view, exceeding their documented role (view applications and manage borrower-facing messages).

The upload allowlist check trusts upload.content_type, a client-controlled header. No magic-byte sniffing or content inspection is performed, so an attacker can upload arbitrary content (e.g. HTML or executables) by declaring an allowed type such as application/pdf.

cwe: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type

extra.message: Uploaded KYC documents (tax returns, government IDs, bank statements) are written verbatim to the local filesystem under storage/uploads with write_bytes(content) and no encryption at rest. Anyone with access to the storage volume or backups can read sensitive borrower documents.

cwe: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information

extra.message: Sensitive borrower financial data is persisted as plaintext columns with no encryption at rest: PaymentAccount.masked_account_number and routing_last4 (models.py:199-200) and BorrowerProfile.tax_identifier_last4/owner_phone (models.py:41-44). A database breach directly exposes this borrower PII and bank-adjacent data.

cwe: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information

extra.message: The ApiKey model has no expires_at column and no lifetime is enforced when keys are authenticated (authenticate_api_key only checks is_active). The API exposes no revocation or rotation endpoint - only creation - so a leaked or stolen API key grants integration access (application status and decision data) indefinitely.

GET /api/applications executes db.scalars(stmt.order_by(...)).all() with no LIMIT or pagination. For admin and support_specialist users application_query_for_user returns every row, so each request loads and serializes the entire applications table, enabling memory/CPU exhaustion as data grows (resource exhaustion).

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: The search parameter q of GET /api/applications is interpolated into the ILIKE pattern f"%{q.strip()}%" without escaping LIKE metacharacters or bounding its length, and is then applied to business_name and purpose. An attacker can submit wildcard-heavy or very long patterns that force expensive full-table pattern matching, degrading database performance for all users.

POST /api/auth/register returns a distinct 409 'Email is already registered' when the submitted email already exists, versus a successful 200 for new emails. The differential response lets an attacker enumerate which email addresses have registered accounts.

In password_reset_request the raw, unhashed password reset token is written to disk: mock_log("email.log", {..., "reset_token": raw_token}) persists the live credential to storage/mock_logs/email.log. Anyone able to read that file can hijack password resets for any account while tokens remain valid.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: GET /api/admin/exports/decisions writes decision fields such as borrower_summary (free text recorded via the decisions API) directly into the CSV response without neutralizing formula characters. A value beginning with '=', '+', '-' or '@' executes as a formula when an admin opens the exported CSV in Excel or Google Sheets (CSV/formula injection).

cwe: CWE-1236: Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File
